builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Dynamic Slack-Aware Clocking for Near-Threshold Tensor Processing Units (TPUs)
summary: The method replaces conservative fixed worst-case global clocking in near-threshold TPUs with per-operation timing tiers predicted from data activity and enforced by local dummy-hold cycles plus a runtime feedback controller. It costs roughly 13% silicon area, predictor and controller design complexity, and about 1% inference accuracy at aggressive operating points. Timing violations from process variation, aging, or mispredicted delay sensitivity can still occur, requiring the closed-loop threshold adaptation to remain correctly tuned.
rationale: This is custom silicon timing design for near-threshold accelerators, which a practitioner limited to a 24 GB GPU or third-party APIs cannot adopt, modify, or benefit from in production.

claims.statement: The method replaces conservative fixed worst-case global clocking in near-threshold TPUs with per-operation timing tiers predicted from data activity and enforced by local dummy-hold cycles plus a runtime feedback controller. It costs roughly 13% silicon area, predictor and controller design complexity, and about 1% inference accuracy at aggressive operating points. Timing violations from process variation, aging, or mispredicted delay sensitivity can still occur, requiring the closed-loop threshold adaptation to remain correctly tuned.
Up to 1.55x better energy efficiency at 2.15x frequency scaling versus a baseline TPU, with approximately 1% average accuracy loss and 13% area overhead.
